mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has been pinned in a narrow -13.7 to -16.9 band for four straight weeks while GROCERY_PHARM stays elevated near +28, so households are still routing spend into essential errands instead of discretionary storefronts. This substitution is still binding and holds RETAIL_REC at or below its last-28-day mean of -14.9 over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is greater than or equal to -14.9 while GROCERY_PHARM remains above +25.

mechanism_narrative: The joint condition of RESIDENTIAL above +6 and GROCERY_PHARM above +27 in the same week means residents are staying home and making only essential errands. Because the two conditions reinforce home confinement, non-essential retail trips are suppressed and RETAIL_REC prints lower over the following four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL weekly mean >= +6.0 and GROCERY_PHARM weekly mean >= +27.0 in the same week
failure_condition: In weeks where RESIDENTIAL >= +6.0 and GROCERY_PHARM >= +27.0 jointly, the following 28-day mean RETAIL_REC is not below the preceding 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT bottomed at -15.1 and has recovered to -10.6, crossing back above the -12 line that separates suppressed trip-taking from partial return to non-essential destinations. Once that crossing prints, discretionary trip intent is restored and RETAIL_REC follows higher within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT weekly mean crosses above -12.0 after being at or below -15.0 in a prior week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT weekly path -13.1, -11.1, -15.1, -10.6 crosses the -12 line at t-0w
failure_condition: Within two weeks of TRANSIT crossing above -12.0, the mean RETAIL_REC is unchanged or lower than the week of the crossing.

mechanism_narrative: The t-1w pattern of PARKS improving 10.3 points, RESIDENTIAL jumping to +10.9 and WORKPLACES collapsing to -32.6 is a holiday-calendar artifact, not a demand shift. Holiday weeks front-load discretionary spending, so the two weeks following the holiday revert to the pre-holiday RETAIL_REC level, at or below the last-28-day mean.
candidate_trigger: PARKS improves by more than 8 points week-on-week while WORKPLACES falls by more than 20 points in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:t-1w PARKS -4.6 vs -14.9 prior, WORKPLACES -32.6 vs -8.6 prior, RESIDENTIAL +10.9 vs +6.7 prior
fact:t-0w PARKS and WORKPLACES revert to -16.9 and -6.4
regime_hint: holiday week followed by post-holiday normalization
failure_condition: Two weeks after the joint holiday signature, mean RETAIL_REC is higher than the t-3w/t-2w mean of -15.5.

mechanism_narrative: Under an active tightening-restrictions regime, transit suppression is the first observable response and retail footfall follows within one week. If TRANSIT falls back to or below -13.0, restrictions are constraining trips again and the next week of RETAIL_REC is lower than its last-28-day mean.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT weekly mean falls to or below -13.0
evidence_refs: fact:t-1w TRANSIT dipped to -15.1 and RETAIL_REC sat at -13.7, its least-negative reading
failure_condition: In the week after TRANSIT prints <= -13.0, RETAIL_REC is higher than or equal to its level in the preceding week.

mechanism_narrative: Setting the holiday week aside, WORKPLACES improved to -6.4 and TRANSIT to -10.6, both the least-negative readings in the window. Joint recovery in commuting and transit mobility signals returning daytime footfall, which lifts RETAIL_REC over the following four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES weekly mean >= -8.0 and TRANSIT weekly mean >= -12.0 in the same non-holiday week
evidence_refs: fact:t-0w WORKPLACES -6.4 and TRANSIT -10.6, both best readings in the four-week window
failure_condition: When WORKPLACES >= -8.0 and TRANSIT >= -12.0 jointly, the following 28-day mean RETAIL_REC is not above the preceding 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: A GROCERY_PHARM weekly mean above +30 marks a stockpiling episode (t-1w printed +34.6) that absorbs household discretionary budget in the immediately following week. The next 7 days of RETAIL_REC therefore print below the stockpiling-week reading.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM = 34.6 at t-1w, above the +30 threshold
fact:RETAIL_REC = -13.7 at t-1w and -15.0 at t-0w
failure_condition: The week after GROCERY_PHARM > +30.0 shows RETAIL_REC higher than the stockpiling week's RETAIL_REC reading.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT at -10.6 and WORKPLACES at -6.4 are simultaneously the most-recovered values of the four-week window, placing mobility at a local maximum. In a reopening regime that is not yet accompanied by RETAIL_REC gains, the level mean-reverts and RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks sits below its last-28-day mean.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both print their least-negative values of the trailing four-week window in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:t-0w TRANSIT -10.6 and WORKPLACES -6.4 are window maxima while RETAIL_REC remains at -15.0
regime_hint: reopening at a mobility local maximum without retail confirmation
failure_condition: When TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both set four-week window maxima, the next 28-day mean RETAIL_REC exceeds the preceding 28-day mean.
